1. Case 1: CHARGE syndrome
The patient is a 7-year-old male with multiple congenital anomalies and dysmorphic features. Key findings include choanal atresia, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with micropenis, bicuspid aortic valve, craniofacial dysmorphism, motor impediment, myopia, conductive hearing loss, and inner ear dysplasia. Crucially, a de novo CHD7 intronic variant was identified, a known genetic cause of CHARGE syndrome. Although coloboma and semicircular canal aplasia/hypoplasia are not documented, which prevents definitive clinical confirmation, the molecular finding and multisystem presentation strongly support CHARGE syndrome. Alternative explanations are less likely: a nonspecific chromosomal/genetic syndrome is refuted by the specific CHD7 variant, and isolated congenital anomalies are refuted by the multisystem involvement and genetic result. Thus, the best diagnosis is CHARGE syndrome.
